### Problem: Interleaving string {#sec-st-p3-inter}

::: {.p-statement}
Return whether `s3` is an interleaving of `s1` and `s2`: a merge that keeps the order of each string and uses every letter exactly once.

On `aabcc`, `dbbca`, `aadbbcbcac` the answer is true. On `aabcc`, `dbbca`, `aadbbbaccc` the answer is false. Three empty strings are true.

Source: [LC 97 · Interleaving String](https://leetcode.com/problems/interleaving-string/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The index in `s3` is `i + j` once `i` letters have been taken from `s1` and `j` from `s2`. The last letter of that prefix came from one of the two strings, and only if that string's next letter equals it. Preferring `s1` whenever both match gets stuck on the first sample: the `b` at position 3 has to come from `s2`. Both choices have to stay alive.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **Reject** unless $|s1| + |s2| = |s3|$.
- **State.** $dp[i][j]$ = the prefix of length $i + j$ of `s3` is an interleaving of the two prefixes.
- **Transition.** OR of "last letter from `s1`" and "last letter from `s2`", each checked against `s3[i + j - 1]`.
- **Base.** $dp[0][0] = \mathrm{true}$. **Answer.** $dp[n][m]$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` asks whether the rest of `s3`, from index `i + j`, can be built from the rest of the two strings. Either string may supply the next letter when it matches.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("inter", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-inter-rec
def inter_rec(a, b, c):
    if len(a) + len(b) != len(c):
        return False

    def f(i, j):
        if i == len(a) and j == len(b):
            return True
        k = i + j
        if i < len(a) and a[i] == c[k] and f(i + 1, j):
            return True
        if j < len(b) and b[j] == c[k] and f(i, j + 1):
            return True
        return False

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool interRec(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b, const string& c) {
    if (i == (int)a.size() && j == (int)b.size()) return true;
    int k = i + j;
    if (i < (int)a.size() && a[i] == c[k] && interRec(i + 1, j, a, b, c)) return true;
    if (j < (int)b.size() && b[j] == c[k] && interRec(i, j + 1, a, b, c)) return true;
    return false;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
A failed branch and a successful one both return to the same `(i, j)`. Store the boolean, including false, so a dead cell is not searched again.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("inter", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-inter-memo
def inter_memo(a, b, c):
    if len(a) + len(b) != len(c):
        return False
    memo = {}

    def f(i, j):
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            if i == len(a) and j == len(b):
                memo[i, j] = True
            else:
                k = i + j
                ok = i < len(a) and a[i] == c[k] and f(i + 1, j)
                ok = ok or (j < len(b) and b[j] == c[k] and f(i, j + 1))
                memo[i, j] = ok
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int interMemo(int i, int j, const string& a, const string& b, const string& c, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (i == (int)a.size() && j == (int)b.size()) return memo[i][j] = 1;
    int k = i + j, ok = 0;
    if (i < (int)a.size() && a[i] == c[k]) ok = interMemo(i + 1, j, a, b, c, memo);
    if (!ok && j < (int)b.size() && b[j] == c[k]) ok = interMemo(i, j + 1, a, b, c, memo);
    return memo[i][j] = ok;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
The corner of an empty merge is true. Each cell looks one step up and one step left, at the letter `c[i + j - 1]`. Replacing OR by addition counts the colourings; the first sample has 3.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("inter", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-inter-tab
def inter_tab(a, b, c):
    if len(a) + len(b) != len(c):
        return False
    n, m = len(a), len(b)
    dp = [[False] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = True
    for i in range(n + 1):
        for j in range(m + 1):
            if i and dp[i - 1][j] and a[i - 1] == c[i + j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = True
            if j and dp[i][j - 1] and b[j - 1] == c[i + j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = True
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool interTab(const string& a, const string& b, const string& c) {
    if (a.size() + b.size() != c.size()) return false;
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<vector<char>> dp(n + 1, vector<char>(m + 1));
    dp[0][0] = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 0; j <= m; ++j) {
            if (i && dp[i - 1][j] && a[i - 1] == c[i + j - 1]) dp[i][j] = 1;
            if (j && dp[i][j - 1] && b[j - 1] == c[i + j - 1]) dp[i][j] = 1;
        }
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### One row

::: {.form-next}
The previous row is `dp` before the iteration of `i`, and the left neighbour is `dp[j]` after it has been written on this row. Update `j` from left to right. A true written at `j - 1` on this row is exactly the left arrow.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("inter", "row")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-inter-row
def inter_row(a, b, c):
    if len(a) + len(b) != len(c):
        return False
    dp = [False] * (len(b) + 1)
    dp[0] = True
    for j in range(1, len(b) + 1):
        dp[j] = dp[j - 1] and b[j - 1] == c[j - 1]
    for i in range(1, len(a) + 1):
        dp[0] = dp[0] and a[i - 1] == c[i - 1]
        for j in range(1, len(b) + 1):
            from_a = dp[j] and a[i - 1] == c[i + j - 1]
            from_b = dp[j - 1] and b[j - 1] == c[i + j - 1]
            dp[j] = from_a or from_b
    return dp[-1]

assert inter_rec("aabcc", "dbbca", "aadbbcbcac") is True
assert inter_memo("aabcc", "dbbca", "aadbbbaccc") is False
assert inter_tab("aabcc", "dbbca", "aadbbcbcac") is True
assert inter_row("aabcc", "dbbca", "aadbbbaccc") is False
assert inter_tab("", "", "") is True
assert inter_row("ab", "aa", "aaba") is True
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool interRow(const string& a, const string& b, const string& c) {
    if (a.size() + b.size() != c.size()) return false;
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<char> dp(m + 1);
    dp[0] = 1;
    for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) dp[j] = dp[j - 1] && b[j - 1] == c[j - 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        dp[0] = dp[0] && a[i - 1] == c[i - 1];
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            bool fromA = dp[j] && a[i - 1] == c[i + j - 1];
            bool fromB = dp[j - 1] && b[j - 1] == c[i + j - 1];
            dp[j] = fromA || fromB;
        }
    }
    return dp[m];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** tries both sources at every tie. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$. **One row** is $O(nm)$ time and $O(\min(n, m))$ memory if the shorter string is the row. Lengths on this problem are small enough for the table; the row is the same algorithm.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Three empty strings: true. The single cell is the base.
- Lengths that do not add: false, before any cell is filled. `a`, `b`, `a` must not read past `s3`.
- Both strings can offer the same letter. The first sample is true only because both branches survive.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- A fixed preference when both strings match. Preferring `s1` fails the first sample. Preferring `s2` fails `ab`, `aa`, `aaba`.
- Skipping the length test. The index `i + j - 1` is then off the end of `s3`, or a longer `s3` is reported true.
- OR replaced by a greedy assignment that consumes a letter forever. The table's OR is the repair.
:::

**Variants.** Counting the colourings is the same table with $+$ and modulo $10^9 + 7$. The first sample has 3 colourings, and `aa` with `aa` into `aaaa` has 6. The minimum number of changes that make `c` some interleaving of `a` and `b` is the same grid with a cost instead of a boolean: [CF 2050E · Three Strings](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/2050/E){rating="1500"}.
